claim: Proposition 2.1
quote: Proposition 2.1 Let T1, T2, . . . , Tn denote the component lifetimes of a series (parallel) system and let relative error in SF due to faulty assumption of components independently working in the series (parallel) system be denoted by ESF(t) (EPF(t)). Then (i) OA(UA) in error assessment of SF for an n component series system is equivalent to the fact that T1, T2, . . . , Tn are PUOD (NUOD). (ii) OA(UA) in error assessment of SF for an n component parallel system is equivalent to the fact that T1, T2, . . . , Tn are PLOD (NLOD).
family: general joint lifetimes T1,...,Tn (no specific family)
compared: dependent system TD vs independent-marginals system TI

hypotheses.text: T1,...,Tn are the component lifetimes of the system

conclusion.direction: equivalence: SF-error sign ⟺ orthant dependence; in order terms, joint survival ≥ product of marginals (PUOD) ⟺ F̄_D ≥ F̄_I ⟺ T_D >=st T_I for series; PLOD ⟺ cdf ordering ⟺ parallel-system st ordering

ambiguity: Printed pairing is 'OA(UA) ↔ PUOD(NUOD)' for series and 'OA(UA) ↔ PLOD(NLOD)' for parallel; given the paper's own convention (ES_F ≥ 0 ⇒ UA), PUOD actually corresponds to UA (ES_F ≥ 0), so the printed OA/UA pairing appears reversed. Also the parallel-system relative error EPF(t) is printed in two inconsistent forms: (F̄_D − F̄_I)/F̄_I and (F̄_I − F̄_D)/F̄_I.

quote: E^F(t) = delta (exp(B(t)) - 1), E^r(t) = -delta B'(t) L / A'(t) [as printed], E^mu(t) = ... [formula]. We conclude that the relative errors in all aforementioned functions are decreasing in t except that for failure rate and AI function it is non-negative constant.
family: Lu and Bhattacharyya (1990) I / Crowder-type model: F_D(t) = exp(A(t) - delta B(t)), B(t) = (sum lambda_i^{1/m} t^{alpha_i/m})^m

conclusion.direction: sign of E^F(t) equals sign of delta (since exp(B(t)) - 1 >= 0): delta > 0 gives UA in SF, i.e. TD >=ST TI per Remark 2.2(i); delta < 0 gives OA, i.e. TD <=ST TI

claim: Section 3.2.6 result: error signs for FGMW series system
